title: Auto Loans: Changing the Monthly Due Day
content:
Borrowers with an Auto Loans account may ask Piedmont Crescent Bank to move the day of the month on which their installments fall due. This policy sets the range, the frequency and the effect of such a change.

## Rule

- **New day.** The new due day is any day from the 1st to the 28th.
- **Size of the move.** The new day may differ from the present one by no more than the product's largest permitted move, in either direction, measured as the gap between the two day numbers within a month.
- **Loan standing.** The loan must be active and have no installment past due, as the loan record shows.
- **Frequency.** Each product allows its stated number of changes within a rolling window of 365 calendar days. A new change is allowed only when 365 calendar days have gone by since the latest change: counting the day after the last change date as day 1, a change is allowed on the day that is the last change date plus 365, and on any day after it. A loan that has never had its due day changed meets this test outright.

## Effect of a change

The next due date moves onto the new day within the same month as the current next due date. Interest keeps accruing day by day, so choosing a later day means the installment carries more interest. The maturity date stays as it was, and no fee is charged for the change.

## Window boundary (hypothetical dates)

A loan whose last due day change was made on 10 June 2030 reaches 365 days on 10 June 2031. A request on 10 June 2031 passes the frequency test; a request on 9 June 2031 does not.

## Effect illustration (hypothetical loan)

A loan due on the 5th with its next installment due 5 April 2031 moves to the 12th: the move is 7 days, and the next due date becomes 12 April 2031, in the same month. Its maturity date and balances do not change.
